statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and M the vertices of maximum degree. Then i(G) ≤ α(G[M)])+ γ(G[V-M])^2.

readings.interpretation: i(G) <= alpha(G[M]) + gamma(G[V-M])^2; G 11-regular so M=V, V-M=empty, gamma(empty)=0

notes: Tight (2<=2). M=V since regular (glossary: M = vertices of maximum degree). Convention gamma(empty graph)=0; no plausible convention makes RHS < 2 since alpha(G[M])=alpha(G)=2 already matches i(G).

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and A the vertices of degree at most n/2. Then i(G) ≤ α(G[A)])+2FLOOR[ Δ(G[V-A])/3].

readings.interpretation: A = {v : deg(v) <= n/2 = 10}; all degrees 11 so A=empty; RHS = alpha(empty) + 2*floor(Delta(G)/3)

notes: A empty under any reading of 'at most n/2' (11 > 10). alpha(empty)=0, G[V-A]=G, Delta=11, 2*floor(11/3)=6 >= 2.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and D the set of vertices each of whose closed neighborhood contains the closed neighborhood of some other vertex. Then i(G) ≤ α(G[V-D])+FLOOR[ (|Ε (G[D])| + 1)/3].

readings.interpretation: D = {v : exists u!=v with N[u] subseteq N[v]}. Same-blob vertices are true twins (N[u]=N[v]), verified computationally, so D=V; RHS = alpha(empty) + floor((|E(G)|+1)/3)

notes: Verified: closed neighborhoods of same-blob vertices identical, so every vertex qualifies for D. RHS=37 >= 2.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices, M its set of maximum degree vertices and A its set of minimum degree vertices. Then i(G) ≤ |E(G[M])| + α(G[N[A]])* α(G[V-A]).

readings.interpretation: Regular graph: M=A=V. |E(G[M])|=|E(G)|=110; N[A]=V; V-A=empty so alpha(G[V-A])=0

notes: First term alone (110) dominates; empty-set convention for the product term irrelevant.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and P the set of pendants of G. Then i(G) ≤ |T_min(G)| + sum of K_4(v)) + γ(G[V-N(P)]).

readings.interpretation: P=empty (no degree-1 vertices); N(P)=empty; V-N(P)=V; T_min(v)=39 (glossary T(v): triangles at a vertex, min over v); sum of K_4(v) = sum over v of #K4s containing v = 20*69

notes: Holds regardless of the K4 term's exact reading: |T_min(G)|=39 >= 2 alone suffices. Vertex-transitivity gives K4(v)=69 for all v (computed at v=0).

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and D the set of neighbor dominators of G. Then i(G) ≤ 4|T_min(G)| + |E(G[D])|

readings.interpretation: Glossary neighbor dominator: v dominates u if N[u] subseteq N[v]; D=V (true twins in blobs, verified). RHS = 4*39 + 110

notes: Holds by huge margin.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and M the vertices of maximum degree. Then i(G) ≤ n - γ(G[N(M)]).

readings.interpretation: M=V (regular); N(M)=N(V)=V (no isolates); gamma(G[V])=gamma(G)=2

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and M the vertices of maximum degree. Then i(G) ≤ |E(C,V-C)| + FLOOR[(2/3)|E(G[V-N(P)])|].

readings.interpretation: C=center=V (all ecc 2), V-C=empty so |E(C,V-C)|=0; P=empty pendants, N(P)=empty, V-N(P)=V, |E(G)|=110

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and C the center of G. Then i(G) ≤ α(G[N(C)])+2 *FLOOR[Caro-Wei -1]

readings.interpretation: C=V, N(C)=V, alpha(G[N(C)])=alpha(G)=2; CW = sum 1/(1+deg) = 20/12 = 5/3 (glossary CW); floor(5/3 - 1) = floor(2/3) = 0

notes: TIGHT: 2 <= 2, zero slack. Exact Fraction arithmetic used for CW.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and C the center of G. Then i(G) ≤ λ_max(G) *residue(G^2 )+ Δ( G[M])

readings.interpretation: lambda_max=2 (max local independence); G^2=K20 (diam 2), residue(K20)=1 (verified by Havel-Hakimi); M=V so Delta(G[M])=11

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and D the set of vertices of degree two of G. Then i(G) ≤ residue(G)+ peN(N(D)) + |T_min(G)|.

readings.interpretation: D = degree-2 vertices = empty (all deg 11); N(D)=empty; peN(empty)=0 (glossary peN: #vertices of V\S with exactly one neighbor in S)

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and A the set of vertices of minimum degree of G. Then i(G) ≤ residue(G)+ γ(G[N[A]]) peN(N(D)) + dp(G), where dp(G) is the number pairs of vertices on the periphery at distance two.

readings.interpretation: Product reading: residue + gamma(G[N[A]])*peN(N(D)) + dp. A=V, N[A]=V, gamma=2; D presumably degree-2 vertices (from 431a) = empty, peN(empty)=0; periphery=V, pairs at distance 2 = nonadjacent pairs = 80
Sum reading (juxtaposition = missing '+'): residue + gamma(G[N[A]]) + peN(N(D)) + dp

notes: D undefined in statement (transcription carries it from 431a: degree-2 vertices, empty here). Holds under both product and sum readings; dp=80 dominates.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then i(G) ≤ residue(G) * |T_max(v)| + dd(G).

readings.interpretation: residue=2, T_max(v)=39 (vertex-transitive), dd = #distinct degrees = 1

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then i(G) ≤ annihilation number + minimum{vertices at even distance from v - vertices at odd distance from v}.

readings.interpretation: dist_even counts v itself (glossary: distance 0 is even, page convention): min over v of (9 - 11) = -2; annihilation=10
dist_even NOT counting v: min over v of (8 - 11) = -3

notes: Holds under both dist_even conventions.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and P the set of pendants of G. Then i(G) ≤ |V-N(P)|+ minimum{vertices at even distance from v - vertices at odd distance from v}*_bipartite.

readings.interpretation: P=empty, N(P)=empty, |V-N(P)|=20; chi_bipartite=0 (girth 3), so second term vanishes under either dist_even convention

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and P the set of pendants of G. Then i(G) ≤ 0.5|N(M)|*FLOOR[2*sum of inverses of degrees of G^2 ].
notes: Exact Fraction arithmetic: 2*(20/19)=40/19, floor=2.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and P the set of pendants of G. Then i(G) ≤ |M| + 2FLOOR[0.5*SW(G^c )].

readings.interpretation: M=V so |M|=20; SW(complement)=8 (complement 8-regular; max core number verified = 8); 2*floor(4)=8

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then i(G) ≤ |M| + 2FLOOR[0.5*SW(G^c )].

readings.interpretation: Same as 434a without pendant clause: |M|=20, SW(G^c)=8

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and M the set of maximum degree vertices of G. Then i(G) ≤ δ( G[ M]) + 1 + SW(G^c ). If diameter > 2, then i(G) ≤ δ( G[ M]) + SW(G^c ).

readings.interpretation: Main clause: G[M]=G, delta=11; SW(G^c)=8. Second clause not applicable (diameter=2)

notes: Sharper diameter>2 clause vacuous here.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and M the set of maximum degree vertices of G. Then i(G) ≤ δ( G[ V-M]) + 1 + SW(G^c ). If δ(G) = 1, then i(G) ≤ δ( G[ V-M]) + SW(G^c ).

readings.interpretation: V-M=empty; convention delta(empty)=0: RHS = 0 + 1 + 8 = 9. Second clause vacuous (delta(G)=11)

notes: delta of empty induced subgraph is a convention issue; with delta(empty)=0 it holds; even any nonnegative convention keeps RHS >= 9 > 2. No plausible reading violates.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and B the set of vertices of maximum eccentricity of G. Then i(G) ≤ SW(G^c ) - c(G[N[B]]) + 2, where c(G[N[B]]) is the number of components of G[N[B]].

readings.interpretation: B=periphery=V (all ecc 2); N[B]=V; G connected so c=1

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices and C the center of G, i.e. the set of vertices of minimum eccentricity of G. Then i(G) ≤ SW(G^c ) - ecc(C) + 2, where ecc(C) is the eccentricity of the set C.

readings.interpretation: Glossary def 52: ecc(S)=max over v in V-S of dist(v,S); C=V so V-C=empty, ecc(V)=0 (max over empty set)
Alternative convention ecc(C)=radius=2 (if set-ecc of V read as vertex eccentricity)

notes: Holds under both conventions for ecc of the full vertex set.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ SW( bar(G) )+CEILING[(1+|E(G^2 [A])|/3], where SW( bar(G) ) is the Szekeres-Wilf invariant of the complement graph of G and E(G^2 [A]) is the edge set of the subgraph of the second power graph of G induced by its minimum degree vertices of G^2.

readings.interpretation: ceil((1+|E|)/3): A = min degree vertices of G^2 = V (K20 regular); |E(G^2[A])|=190; RHS = 8 + ceil(191/3) = 8+64 = 72
ceil(1+|E|/3) (bracket ambiguity): 8 + ceil(1+190/3) = 8 + 65 = 73

notes: A=V whether 'minimum degree vertices' is read in G (regular) or in G^2 (K20). alpha_2 verified by ILP = 4.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ k* WP( bar(G) ) + Δ(G[D]), where Δ(G[D]) is the maximum degree of the subgraph induced by the nighbor dominators and k is the kth step for a zero in the Havil-Hakimi process.

readings.interpretation: k = HH steps to first zero on G's degree sequence = 17 (verified); WP(barG)=12 (all comp degrees 8, max k with k+8<=20); D = neighbor dominators = V (true twins), Delta(G[D])=11

notes: Also holds under the [DP12] partial result alpha_k <= WP(barG)+k-1 framing.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ a(G) + a(G[V-A]) + |E(G[A])|, where A is the set of vertices of minimum degree of G.

readings.interpretation: a = alpha (independence, per invariants field): A=V, V-A=empty; RHS = 2 + 0 + 110 = 112
a = annihilation number: RHS = 10 + 0 + 110 = 120

notes: |E(G[A])|=|E(G)|=110 dominates under either reading of a().

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ a(G) + a(G[V-H_2 ]) + |E(G[H_2 ])|, where H_2 is the set of vertices of degree at most 2 in G.

readings.interpretation: a = alpha: H_2=empty (all deg 11), V-H_2=V; RHS = alpha(G)+alpha(G)+0 = 2+2+0 = 4
a = annihilation: RHS = 10+10+0 = 20

notes: TIGHT under the alpha reading: 4 <= 4, zero slack. Both readings hold.

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ |N(M)| + FLOOR[2(CW(G) -1)], where M is the set of maximum degree vertices and CW(G) is the Caro-Wei invariant of G.
Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ n - CEILING[path(G[H_3 ])/2, where H_3 is the set of vertices of degree at least 3 in G.

readings.interpretation: H_3=V (all deg 11); path(G)=4 (largest induced path, verified: induced P4 exists, P5 does not); RHS = 20 - ceil(4/2) = 18

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ sum of disparities - |N(A_c )| -2, where A_c is the intersection of all maximum independent sets of G.

readings.interpretation: disp(v)=1 for all v (regular: neighbors all deg 11), sum=20; A_c = alphacore = empty (80 MIS, empty intersection, verified); N(empty)=empty

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ n - FLOOR[dd(K_4(v))/2], where dd(K_4(v)) is the number of distinct values that appear in the sequence of the number of K_4 incident to a vertex.

readings.interpretation: Vertex-transitive: K_4(v)=69 for all v, so dd=1; floor(1/2)=0; RHS = 20

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ p Ν(Α) + |V\S|, where A is the set of minimum degree vertices and S is the set of support vertices.

readings.interpretation: pN(A) private neighbors (glossary pN(S): #vertices of V(G) with exactly one neighbor in S): A=V, pN(V)= #degree-1 vertices = 0; S=empty (no pendants), |V\S|=20; RHS = 0+20 = 20
p * |N(A)| (path cover times neighborhood size): 1*20 + 20 = 40

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ |H_n/2 | + |E(G[V-H_n/2 ])| + ρ(G), where H_n/2 is the set of vertices of degree greater than n/2 in G.

rho = 2-packing number = 1 (diameter 2)

statement: Let G be a connected graph on n > 3 vertices. Then α_2(G) ≤ |V-A| + |E(G[N(S)])| + ρ(G), where A is the set of vertices of minimum degree and S is the set of support vertices in G.

rho = 2-packing number (standard rho(G) in domination theory): diameter 2 so packing = 1
rho = radius (rho sometimes denotes rad): rad = 2
rho = domination number gamma: 2
